newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World airports see passenger, cargo rise in May.
newsitem.headline: World airports see passenger, cargo rise in May.

text.p: World airports on Monday reported a rise in May of six per cent in passenger traffic and eight per cent in cargo over the same month last year.

Figures issued by the Geneva-based Airports Council International (ACI) also showed a steady rise of seven per cent in passengers and four per cent in cargo over the first five months of 1996 against the same period in 1995.
The main passenger surge in May was in North America where travellers through airports totalled 105,8 million in May -- 7.5 per cent more than in May, 1995.
The Asia/Pacific region saw a rise of 6.9 per cent to 29,9 million passengers and Europe's airports handled 62,6 million people, an increase of 4.5 per cent.

North America also saw a rise of 10.5 per cent in cargo for a total of 2,2 million metric tonnes. Asia/Pacific airports handled 830,725 metric tonnes, an increase of six per cent, and European airports 819,626 tonnes -- up 4.8 per cent.
The Middle East also saw a strong cargo surge of 12.9 per cent, but from a low base. The May tonnage was 127,242, ACI reported.
ACI, which issues the figures monthly, based its latest report on returns from 460 airports worldwide.
Top three world passenger airports remained Chicago with 5,9 million, Atlanta with 5.7 million and Los Angeles with 4,8 million.
Atlanta, which saw its passenger numbers climb 17.1 per cent during the month, has had its transit rates boosted steadily during 1996 because of the Olympic Games which it hosted in July and August.

Top cargo airports remained Memphis with 173,829 tonnes, an increase of 23.5 per cent over May 1995, Los Angeles with 143,451 tonnes, a rise of 11,9 per cent, and Miami, which recorded 139,287 tonnes -- a 0.1 percentage drop.
